issues.legal_issue: A court retaining control of a specific performance suit may extend the time for a purchaser to deposit the amount required to complete the contract, even after the original deadline has passed.
material_facts: The trial court decreed specific performance and directed the purchaser to deposit the outstanding mortgage amount by a specified deadline, but she did not deposit it in time.
The High Court vacated the clause that would automatically dismiss the suit for failure to deposit by the deadline, but later rescinded the contract.
The purchaser sought further time and credit for money she had paid to the mortgagee, and the Supreme Court granted an opportunity to deposit the amount required by the trial court.
issues.conclusion: The court could extend the time for deposit. It granted additional time, subject to equitable conditions, rather than allowing the contract to be rescinded outright.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 28 of the Specific Relief Act, a specific performance decree is, for practical purposes, a preliminary decree: the suit remains under the court’s control until a party applies for a final decree. The court may extend the time for deposit; the relief is equitable and may be granted on terms that do equity to the opposite party.

predicates.specific_performance_proceeding: The proceeding seeks enforcement of an agreement by specific performance.
predicates.deposit_deadline_missed: The purchaser did not deposit the amount required by the decree within the time originally allowed.
predicates.suit_remained_under_court_control: The suit remained before the court for further steps toward a final decree.

issues.definition: When a specific performance proceeding remains under the court’s control after the purchaser misses the original deposit deadline, the court may extend the time for deposit.

issues.legal_issue: A purchaser seeking equitable specific performance after taking an assignment of the vendor’s mortgage rights instead of discharging the mortgage may be required to surrender those rights as a condition of relief.
material_facts: The agreement required the purchaser to pay the outstanding mortgage amount, and she had paid the rest of the consideration and received possession.
After missing the court-ordered deposit deadline, the purchaser paid the mortgagee and took an assignment of its mortgage rights rather than extinguishing the mortgage.
She obtained a mortgage decree against the vendor and sought specific performance while retaining rights under that decree.
The Supreme Court considered the assignment inconsistent with the agreement and capable of giving the purchaser an unrighteous advantage over the vendor.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser could obtain specific performance only if she deposited the required consideration with interest and undertook to give up her rights under the mortgage decree, except for the amount actually paid to obtain the assignment.
issues.legal_principle: Specific performance is an equitable relief, and a person seeking equity must do equity. The court may impose terms to prevent a party from retaining an advantage obtained through conduct inconsistent with the contractual understanding.

rule.if: seeks_specific_performance and purchaser_bound_to_discharge_mortgage and purchaser_took_assignment_instead_of_extinguishing_mortgage and assignment_created_rights_against_vendor

predicates.seeks_specific_performance: The purchaser asks the court to enforce an agreement for sale.
predicates.purchaser_bound_to_discharge_mortgage: The purchaser is responsible under the agreement for paying off an existing mortgage on the property.
predicates.purchaser_took_assignment_instead_of_ext: The purchaser obtained an assignment of the mortgage rights rather than simply discharging the mortgage.
predicates.assignment_created_rights_against_vendor: The assigned mortgage rights enabled the purchaser to assert a mortgage claim against the vendor.

issues.definition: When a purchaser seeking specific performance takes mortgage rights against the vendor instead of extinguishing a mortgage the purchaser was bound to discharge, relief may be conditioned on surrendering those rights, apart from the amount actually paid.
